title: A Salt for the Garden
premise: Vesper Villalobos, a meticulous cartographer who maps realms that should not exist, discovers that the guild ledgers he keeps record debts paid in souls. The dying stranger's map is a deed of ownership: Vesper's own soul, sold generations ago by an ancestor and now claimed by the court beneath the mountain. To free himself, Vesper must steal back not only his soul but the soul of the stranger's daughter, held as collateral, before the court's tithe-night seals both bargains forever. He succeeds only by redrawing the map of the underworld itself — sacrificing the guild's immortality-ledgers and, with them, his last claim to belonging — and returns to the surface changed: a man with no recorded name, finally free to make his own.
about_author: Odile Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging estate ledgers in provincial libraries, where she first noticed how often inheritance and debt entangle. She writes fantasy about people caught in paperwork older than themselves.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. He catalogs an impossible delivery — a jar of bottled dusk — while balancing the guild's ledgers, establishing his meticulous, detached life. A clerk mocks his lack of family name. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as order.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Ink Door
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A bleeding stranger staggers into the guild's map room at closing, presses a folded map into Vesper's hands, and dies whispering 'the tithe is due.' Vesper's fingerprints are on the deed. Beat: fear and unwilling inheritance.

chapters.title: Ledgers Written in Salt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with a brief ledger-entry interlude. He discovers the guild's accounts record souls as currency — and his own name appears as an asset, sold by an ancestor named Villalobos. Beat: identity collapses; the map he keeps is a cage.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Guild Objects
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The guild master, Seraphine Quill, coldly confirms the debt and offers to buy Vesper's cooperation — he'll be erased, not saved. He refuses and flees with the map. Beat: betrayal by the only institution he belonged to.

chapters.title: What the Dying Man Owed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Following the map's first clue, he finds the stranger's daughter, Ilsa, half-faded — her soul already partially claimed. She reveals her father tried to buy her back and failed. Beat: reluctant alliance, shared stakes.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember Feet
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The road to the mountain rearranges itself, testing travelers with memories of home. Ilsa watches Vesper fail the test — he has no warm memory to offer. Beat: pity turning to respect for his stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At a border shrine, a ferry-creature demands a name as passage. Vesper pays with his guild title, severing his last official identity. Beat: grief and strange lightness — losing what never truly fit.

chapters.title: A Market of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. They pass through a bazaar trading lifespans and regrets. Vesper trades a year of his life for a map of the underworld's upper galleries. Beat: temptation, and the first hint Vesper is becoming someone new.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They reach the obsidian gates; the court's herald recognizes the deed and mockingly welcomes 'the asset' home. Vesper sees the ledger hall where his soul sits filed like grain. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Guests of the Undermountain
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The court hosts them with poisonous courtesy while tithe-night preparations proceed. Vesper studies the archive's geography, memorizing what no map has ever shown. Beat: the hunter learning the hunt.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Souls
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. He befriends the court's archivist, a centuries-old clerk who filed Vesper's ancestor's original sale — and who despises the system she serves. She hints at a flaw: souls can be redrawn, like maps. Beat: hope with a cost attached.

chapters.title: Tithe-Night Eve
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Preparations for the tithe; Ilsa's fading accelerates. She and Vesper admit what belonging means to each of them — she lost a family, he never had one. Beat: tenderness before danger; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: The First Theft
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. He attempts to steal his own soul-file and triggers the archive's defenses — the ledgers scream his name. He escapes with only a fragment: the page proving his ancestor was coerced. Beat: failure, but a weapon gained.

chapters.title: The Bargain Seraphine Kept
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Flashback and present: the guild master arrives beneath the mountain to negotiate — she sold Vesper's location to the court in exchange for the guild's exemption. Beat: the true depth of institutional betrayal revealed.

chapters.title: Salt for the Garden
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The archivist explains the title's riddle: salt preserves and kills; a soul redrawn in salt cannot be owned, but its bearer cannot be mapped again — ever. Vesper accepts. Beat: the choice that defines the book.

chapters.title: The Court Wakes
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The theft discovered, the court hunts them through shifting galleries. Ilsa, nearly transparent, buys time by claiming her father's debt publicly, forcing a hearing. Beat: courage from the fading girl.

chapters.title: A Hearing Before the Mountain
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Before the court, Vesper presents the coercion evidence, arguing the original sale was void. The court counters: debts transfer, innocence doesn't matter. Seraphine testifies against him. Beat: the legal climax's first blow.

chapters.title: The Redrawing
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Denied justice, Vesper acts during the tithe itself: he redraws the underworld's master map in salt, unmaking the court's claim-lines. The mountain shudders; souls loosen like moored boats. Beat: climax — creation as rebellion.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Owes
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. In the collapse, the court's herald is unmade by its own ledger; Ilsa's soul snaps back into her body. Vesper, unmappable and unclaimed, is cast out — but the freed souls follow him upward. Beat: triumph laced with exile.

chapters.title: The Guild Without Ledgers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. He returns to find Seraphine ruined — the guild's soul-ledgers burned by the redrawing's backlash. She asks what he'll do; he answers: keep mapping, for free. Beat: mercy as the final victory over his old life.

chapters.title: A Name of His Own
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. On the road home, Ilsa asks Vesper what to call him now. He chooses 'Vesper' — not the inherited name, but the evening star, the first light in the dark. Beat: identity self-authored at last.

chapters.title: The Unmapped Coast
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue. Months later, Vesper and Ilsa run a small atelier drawing honest maps for ordinary travelers. A sealed envelope arrives bearing the guild's old seal — and Vesper smiles, ready. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; the door left open for more.
